definition: The flow of electric charge. In metals, this is the flow of electrons. Measured in amperes (A). I = Q/t.
clues: This is a quantity measured in physics
It describes the flow of electric charge
It is measured in amperes
The rate of flow of charge — in metals, negative electrons flow from negative to positive; measured in amps using an ammeter

definition: The energy transferred per unit charge between two points in a circuit. Also called voltage. Measured in volts (V). V = W/Q.
clues: This is a quantity measured in physics
It is also called voltage
It is measured in volts
The energy transferred per coulomb of charge — V = W/Q; measured across components using a voltmeter in parallel

definition: The opposition to the flow of current in a circuit. Measured in ohms (Ω). R = V/I.
clues: This is a property of components in a circuit
It opposes the flow of current
It is measured in ohms
The opposition to current flow — R = V/I; higher resistance means less current flows for a given voltage

definition: The current through a conductor is directly proportional to the potential difference across it, provided temperature remains constant. V = IR.
clues: This is a law in physics
It relates current, voltage and resistance
It applies to resistors at constant temperature
V = IR — current is proportional to voltage at constant temperature; components that obey this are called ohmic conductors

definition: A circuit where components are connected in a single loop. Current is the same everywhere; voltages add up; total resistance is the sum of individual resistances.
clues: This is a type of electrical circuit
Components are connected in a single loop
The current is the same through all components
A single-loop circuit — same current throughout, voltages divide across components, total resistance = sum of all resistances

definition: A circuit where components are connected across the same two points. Voltage is the same across each branch; currents add up; total resistance is lower than any individual resistance.
clues: This is a type of electrical circuit
Components are connected across the same two points
The voltage is the same across each branch
A circuit with multiple branches — same voltage across each branch, currents add up, total resistance is lower than any single branch

definition: An instrument used to measure electric current. Connected in series in a circuit. Has very low resistance.
clues: This is a measuring instrument in circuits
It measures electric current
It is always connected in series
A device measuring current in amps — always placed in series in a circuit and has very low resistance to avoid affecting the circuit

definition: An instrument used to measure potential difference (voltage). Connected in parallel across a component. Has very high resistance.
clues: This is a measuring instrument in circuits
It measures potential difference
It is always connected in parallel
A device measuring voltage — connected in parallel across a component; has very high resistance so it barely affects the circuit

definition: A resistor whose resistance decreases as its temperature increases. Used in thermostats and temperature sensors.
clues: This is a type of electrical component
Its resistance changes with temperature
As temperature increases, its resistance decreases
A component whose resistance falls as temperature rises — used in temperature sensors and thermostats

definition: Light-dependent resistor — a component whose resistance decreases as light intensity increases. Used in automatic lighting systems.
clues: This is a type of electrical component
Its resistance changes with light level
As light increases, its resistance decreases
Light-dependent resistor — resistance falls in bright light, rises in darkness; used in automatic lights and burglar alarms

definition: A component that allows current to flow in only one direction. Has very high resistance in the reverse direction.
clues: This is a type of electrical component
It only allows current to flow in one direction
It has very high resistance when connected the wrong way round
A component that permits current in one direction only — used to convert AC to DC and in LED displays

definition: Light-emitting diode — a diode that emits light when current flows through it. More efficient than filament bulbs.
clues: This is a type of electrical component
It emits light when current flows through it
It is more efficient than a traditional light bulb
A diode that produces light — more energy-efficient than filament bulbs; used in displays, lighting and remote controls

definition: A fundamental property of matter. Measured in coulombs (C). Q = It. Like charges repel; unlike charges attract.
clues: This is a fundamental property in physics
It is measured in coulombs
Like types of it repel; unlike types attract
A property of particles — Q = It (charge = current × time); electrons carry negative charge, protons carry positive charge

definition: The SI unit of electric charge. Symbol: C. The charge that passes when a current of 1 ampere flows for 1 second.
clues: This is a unit of measurement in physics
It is the unit of electric charge
1 amp flowing for 1 second gives 1 of these
The SI unit of charge — 1 C passes when a current of 1 A flows for 1 second; Q = It

definition: Alternating current — electric current that periodically reverses direction. Mains electricity in the UK is AC at 50 Hz and 230 V.
clues: This is a type of electric current
It repeatedly reverses direction
The UK mains supply is this type
Alternating current — reverses direction 50 times per second (50 Hz) in the UK; produced by generators

definition: Direct current — electric current that flows in one direction only. Produced by batteries and solar cells.
clues: This is a type of electric current
It flows in one direction only
Batteries produce this type
Direct current — flows in a single direction; produced by batteries, solar cells and electronic power supplies

definition: The wire in a mains cable that carries the alternating potential difference (230 V in the UK). Colour: brown.
clues: This is a wire in a mains plug
It carries the supply voltage
Its colour is brown
The brown wire in a mains plug — it carries the 230 V alternating potential difference; touching it when live is extremely dangerous

definition: The wire in a mains cable that completes the circuit, returning current to the power supply. Colour: blue.
clues: This is a wire in a mains plug
It completes the circuit
Its colour is blue
The blue wire in a mains plug — it returns current to the supply and is at approximately 0 V

definition: A safety wire in a mains cable that connects the metal casing of an appliance to the ground, preventing electric shock. Colour: green and yellow.
clues: This is a safety wire in a mains plug
It is connected to the metal case of an appliance
It prevents electric shock
The green and yellow wire — it connects metal appliance casings to earth; if a fault occurs, current flows safely to earth rather than through the user

definition: A safety device containing a thin wire that melts and breaks the circuit if the current exceeds a safe level, preventing damage or fire.
clues: This is a safety device in electrical circuits
It contains a thin wire that melts under excess current
It protects appliances and wiring from damage
A thin wire in a protective casing — melts and breaks the circuit if too much current flows, preventing fire and damage

definition: The rate at which electrical energy is transferred. P = IV or P = I²R or P = V²/R. Measured in watts.
clues: This is a quantity in physics measured in watts
It is the rate of electrical energy transfer
It can be calculated using current and voltage
The rate of transferring electrical energy — P = IV; a 2 kW kettle transfers 2000 J of energy every second

definition: A unit of energy equal to the energy transferred by a 1 kW device in 1 hour. Used for billing electricity. 1 kWh = 3,600,000 J.
clues: This is a unit of energy used in everyday life
It is used on electricity bills
It equals the energy used by a 1 kW device for one hour
The unit on electricity bills — 1 kWh = 3.6 MJ; calculated as power (kW) × time (hours)

definition: Electric charge that builds up on the surface of insulating materials when they are rubbed together, transferring electrons from one material to the other.
clues: This is a type of electrical phenomenon
It is caused by rubbing insulating materials together
Electrons are transferred between surfaces
A build-up of electric charge on the surface of an insulator — caused by friction transferring electrons; can cause sparks or attract dust

definition: The region around a charged object in which other charged objects experience a force. Represented by field lines pointing from positive to negative.
clues: This is a region in physics where forces act
It surrounds charged objects
Field lines point from positive to negative
The region around a charged object where forces act on other charges — field lines show direction of force on a positive test charge

definition: A device that uses electromagnetic induction to change the voltage of an AC supply. Step-up transformers increase voltage; step-down reduce it.
clues: This is a device that changes voltage
It only works with alternating current
Step-up and step-down are the two types
Uses electromagnetic induction to change AC voltage — step-up increases it for transmission, step-down decreases it for safe domestic use

definition: Standardised symbols used to represent electrical components in circuit diagrams, such as cells, resistors, diodes, LEDs and switches.
clues: These are used in circuit diagrams
Each one represents a different component
They are internationally standardised
Internationally agreed symbols used to draw circuits — e.g. a zigzag line for a resistor, a circle with a cross for a bulb
